speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand what is happening, tell me, were any of these bleeding episodes triggered by injury, or did they start spontaneously?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: ITP (Immune Thrombocytopenia)

The child is a 4-year-old male with spontaneous mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae on the distal extremities; please provide the complete blood count (CBC) and platelet count results immediately.
